title: Invertible modules give a representable open locus in coherent families
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper flat morphism of schemes of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $\mathcal C_f$ be the category of quasi-coherent finitely presented modules flat over the test scheme with proper support, with pullback isomorphisms as arrows, specified in [lem-sfb-coherent-stack-algebraic-lfp]. Let $\mathcal B_f(T)$ be the groupoid of invertible modules on $X_T=X\times_ST$ with the same arrows [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-base-change, def-pc-module-pullback]. Forgetting invertibility defines a fully faithful morphism $\mathcal B_f\to\mathcal C_f$ representable by open immersions [def-sfb-open-moduli-substack]. Explicitly, for every $T\to S$ and every $F\in\mathcal C_f(T)$ there is an open subscheme $U_F\subseteq T$ such that, for every scheme morphism $v:T_1\to T$, the pullback $v_X^*F$ is invertible if and only if $v$ factors through $U_F$. The two-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal C_f}\mathcal B_f$ is represented by this open subscheme. No assumption on geometric reducedness or on $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is imposed.

proof.text: First the forgetful map is defined. For every $T\to S$, $p=f_T:X_T\to T$ is flat and proper by the two base-change lemmas. A line bundle $L$ is locally $\mathcal O_{X_T}$, hence is quasi-coherent and finitely presented and its stalk is free of rank one over the corresponding structure stalk. That stalk is flat over the base stalk since $p$ is flat, which by the definition of a flat morphism means that each $\mathcal O_{X_T,x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,p(x)}$; the transitivity lemma (or the rank-one identification itself) gives flatness of $L$ over $T$. Its proper support in the precise ambient convention is witnessed by $Z=X_T$, $i=\mathrm{id}$ and $G=L$. Thus it is an object of $\mathcal C_f(T)$. Pullback replaces a frame $\mathcal O$ by $\mathcal O$ via the tensor formula, so invertibility is stable under every pullback. Both groupoids use exactly the same pullback isomorphisms as arrows, giving full faithfulness.

Fix $F\in\mathcal C_f(T)$. The morphism $p$ is locally of finite presentation by clause (3) of the permanence lemma, because $f$ is of finite presentation. The ambient statement supplies finite presentation and $T$-flatness of $F$. Apply the relative finite-free-locus lemma to obtain an open $W=W(F)\subseteq X_T$ with $W(v_X^*F)=v_X^{-1}(W)$ for every $v:T_1\to T$. Put $Z=|X_T|\setminus W$ and $V=T\setminus p(Z)$. Since $p$ is proper it is a closed map, directly by the definition of universally closed; hence $V$ is open and $X_V$ lies in $W$. Consequently $E=F|_{X_V}$ is finite locally free.

We will use the following point lifting explicitly. If $x\in X_T$ and $t_1\in T_1$ satisfy $p(x)=v(t_1)=t$, choose a common extension field $M$ of $\kappa(x)$ and $\kappa(t_1)$ over $\kappa(t)$ by the common-extension-fields lemma. The resulting maps $\operatorname{Spec}M\to X_T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}M\to T_1$ have the same composite to $T$, namely the residue point at $t$ followed by the same field embedding. The universal property of the scheme fibre product gives a point of $X_T\times_TT_1$ above both $x$ and $t_1$. Thus $v(T_1)\cap p(Z)=\varnothing$ if and only if $v_X^{-1}(Z)=\varnothing$. Together with Step 2 this proves: $v_X^*F$ is finite locally free if and only if $v$ factors through $V$. Here a map with image in an open factors uniquely by restricting its continuous map and its structure-sheaf map to that open; its local stalk maps are unchanged.

On $X_V$ choose local finite frames for $E$. The number of basis vectors is independent of the frame: at a point reduce the two frames modulo the maximal ideal to get two bases of the same residue vector space. It is locally constant because a frame works throughout its open domain. Hence the rank-one locus $R\subseteq X_V$ is open, and its complement $C$ is open as a union of frame neighbourhoods with rank different from one; thus $C$ is also closed. Pullback of a frame of rank $r$ is a frame of rank $r$ by $\mathcal O\otimes\mathcal O^{\oplus r}=\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$. Equality of residue dimensions is preserved under extension of residue fields by the finite-dimensional base-change lemma. In particular a point above $x$ has rank one exactly when $x$ does. This is the rank decomposition in 0D03, using only frames; no finiteness of the total set of ranks is needed.

proof.text: The morphism $p_V:X_V\to V$ is proper by base change. Therefore $p_V(C)$ is closed and $U=V\setminus p_V(C)$ is open in $V$, hence in $T$. If $v:T_1\to T$ pulls $F$ back to an invertible module, Step 3 factors $v$ through $V$. For this factorization the pullback has rank one everywhere, so Step 4 says that the inverse image of $C$ is empty. Point lifting from Step 3, now over $V$, says precisely that $v(T_1)$ misses $p_V(C)$, so $v$ factors through $U$. Conversely a factorization through $U$ has image missing $p_V(C)$ and pulls $E$ back only from $R$. Pulling back its rank-one frames proves that $v_X^*F$ is invertible. Factorizations through $U$ are unique by the open-subscheme description used in Step 3.

For a test map $v:T_1\to T$, the two-fibre product has objects consisting of a line bundle $L$ on $X_{T_1}$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:L\simeq v_X^*F$ (reverse it if the comma convention chooses the opposite orientation). If $v$ factors through $U$, take $(v_X^*F,\mathrm{id})$. Every other object has a unique arrow to this one, namely $\alpha$; compatibility with the displayed isomorphisms forces that arrow and forces every automorphism to be the identity. If there is no factorization through $U$, Step 5 says there is no such object. These equivalences are natural under pullback: the distinguished object pulls back to the distinguished object via the pullback-composition isomorphism, and the unique arrows force compatibility. Together with the unique open factorization they identify the two-fibre product over $T$ with $h_U$. Thus the fully faithful map is representable by open immersions in the stated definition. Neither geometric reducedness nor a statement about $f_*\mathcal O_X$ entered the argument.
